I’m on week 4 of body recomp right now. I’m loving it so far because like you said it feels so sustainable. 
I have a low body fat % but never liked how I looked because of low muscle mass, I look ‘skinny fat’. So I always tried to restrict my calories in the past which never lasted. I didn’t realise I actually needed to be eating more (at maintenance) and lifting weights (heavy and close to failure). 
I actually enjoy eating now! 
And the gym is hard but it feels rewarding. I haven’t noticed any physical changes yet (obv I’m very early) but I’m already noticing things like my posture is better.  
I think the hardest part is that it’s just a slow process and I struggle with perfectionism so I always wonder if there’s something I’m not doing right, something I need to change etc. And it’s the opposite of instant gratification since you have to put in the work over a long period of time before you start seeing any results.

11:29 your core opens up before the legs start going: make sure you keep that forward position instead through the leg drive, then open up the body, then pull in the arms. It's a quads-heavy exercise, your legs should get tired before anything else. Arms only, then arms-body, then half legs, then full legs is a good warmup routine to get that separation down. Also try and keep the handle at constant height, ideally the chain always being within the top half of the cage. Lastly, some strokes seemed longer than others (at 11:31 you stay quite short): make sure you lengthen consistently not to lose useful space. Compress until your shins are circa perpendicular to the ground, that's usually a good strong position to start pushing.

It's a bit of a tricky exercise (still not as tricky as the real thing though!) and most non-rowers do it incorrectly. Be patient with it and keep focusing on technique. The first big shift happens when you can start feeling the legs driving the movement, then a second big shift when you can relax the shoulders, not overcompress and be strong at the catch. Doing it in 15-20 minute sessions with 2-3reps and focusing on technique really helps.
